newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan people march against social disorder.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan people march against social disorder.

text.p: More than 20,000 demonstrators marched toward the presidential office on Sunday to protest against President Lee Teng-hui's failure to replace the premier immediately in response to growing concerns about crime.

"Apologise, President (Lee)! Step down, Premier (Lien Chan)!" the throng shouted as they gathered and started the march, the second major protest this month demanding the government improve social order.

"The best way for President Lee is to replace premier immediately to show his concrete apology," said Lin Yi-hsiung, spokesman for the protest and a prominent member of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party.
"I come hear to listen to people's voice," government spokesman David Lee said in a live television broadcast of the march.
"What they (people) worry most is the safety of women and childen...if they don't feel safe, that's our (the cabinet) fault."
President Lee on Thursday took the blame for what he called Taiwan's worsening social order and gave the green light for his hand-picked premier to quit in July.

"We are very disappointed by the so-called presidential news conference during which Lee failed to really apologise to the public and replace the cabinet head immediately," protest's major organiser Li Tien-chien had said.

Premier Lien and his cabinet face fierce critcism over violent crimes that investigators have failed to crack, including the gangland-style execution of a county magistrate and seven colleagues and the kidnap-murder of an actress' daughter.
Lien offered to resign in July after completion of constitutional amendments by the National Assembly.
Lee accepted the blame in his news conference, saying he felt saddened that the crimes had bred fear.

But Li, executive secretary of the Humanistic Educational Foundation which organised the march, said the president gave no concrete plans to address the public's needs, and to protect the safety of women and children.
Organisers had expected more 20,000 people from about 500 groups to participate in the march. All particpating groups have signed agreements to launch a rational and peaceful march.
Some 50,000 people took to the street in a mass protest organised by Li's group on May 4, demanding a cabinet reshuffle and improvement of social order in Taiwan.
They claimed they had been living in a state of fear because the government failed to improve the social order.
